name: Calibration of long-stem standard platinum resistance thermometers at the ITS-90 triple point of argon (83.8058 K) in a liquid-nitrogen-cooled sealed argon cell (Isotech Model 471)
plain_name: Calibrate a precision platinum thermometer at the melting point of frozen argon
description: A sealed argon cell is frozen with liquid nitrogen poured through its re-entrant well. The SPRT is then calibrated on the melting plateau, which lasts about 4 h. Isotech states k=2 uncertainty of 0.5 mK; NIST lists 0.14 mK for its own realization.
keywords: Calibrate a precision platinum thermometer at the melting point of frozen argon

sources.citation: Tavener, Argon Triple Point - Isotech Model 471, Isotech Seminar 2018

requirements.rationale: The calibration point is the argon triple point, 83.8058 K.
The argon has to be frozen, so the apparatus must cool below the triple point.
The Isotech procedure freezes the cell with LN2. NIST also has a closed-cycle apparatus, so LN2 is not mandatory.
